messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a strong prescription combination pain medicine containing an opioid, hydrocodone, in addition to acetaminophen, which is used to manage moderate to moderately severe pain, when other pain treatments such as non-opioid pain medicines do not treat your pain well enough, or you cannot tolerate them.
An opioid pain medicine that can put you at risk for overdose and death. Even if you take your dose correctly as prescribed, you are at risk for opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse that can lead to death. Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a Schedule II controlled substance.
All branded hydrocodone and acetaminophen (Norco, Vicodin, Lortab, Hycet, Lorcet, Verdrocet, Xodol, Zamicet) have been discontinued, but generic hydrocodone and acetaminophen tablets and oral solution is still available.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen first gained FDA approval on May 3, 1982.
Triplet: ["hydrocodone and acetaminophen", "has brand names", "Xodol"]

The relation 'has brand names' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject medication is available under the brand names listed in the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has brand name': The subject drug is marketed under the brand or trade name specified by the object entity.
B. 'distributed from': The subject drug brand is distributed or licensed from the company specified by the object entity.
C. 'manufactured by': The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.
D. 'has generic version availability': The subject drug is available in generic formulations, as indicated by the object entity.
E. 'has generic name': The subject drug is sold under or known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
